--> VITALS : The Timberwolves look to complete a sweep of the Sunshine State after annihilating the Miami Heat on Wednesday 131-106. Orlando is hoping to get on the board after falling to division rival Atlanta 132-125 despite 35 points and 10 assists from Paolo Banchero. 
 The Magic led by a point entering the fourth quarter, having scored 100 through three in Sean Sweeney’s debut as head coach. Although the team did erase a 10-point halftime deficit, it ultimately wasted an efficient 10-for-12 shooting game from Banchero due to 20 turnovers, a 34-22 bench-scoring deficit and a defensive effort that allowed 48.9 percent shooting against the Hawks.

Although the team did erase a 10-point halftime deficit, it ultimately wasted an efficient 10-for-12 shooting game from Banchero due to 20 turnovers, a 34-22 bench-scoring deficit and a defensive effort that allowed 48.9 percent shooting against the Hawks.
 Minnesota got nine 3-pointers from Anthony Edwards, who scored 45 points to establish himself as the NBA’s scoring leader after every team’s debut. LaMelo Ball added 21 points and a team-high six assists for the Timberwolves in his first contest after arriving from Charlotte and chipped in five of the team’s 21 3-point makes. Slowing Edwards and Ball down will be made tougher by the continued absence of guard Anthony Black (ankle), who has been ruled out.

Slowing Edwards and Ball down will be made tougher by the continued absence of guard Anthony Black (ankle), who has been ruled out.
 Orlando owns a 46-27 edge against the Timberwolves in this matchup between two of the league’s most recent expansion teams. The Magic swept last season’s meetings, which were both played earlier this year. Following a 119-92 rout in Minneapolis on March 7, the Magic defeated the Wolves 132-120 in the most recent matchup on April 8, overcoming 33 points from wing Terrance Shannon Jr. Banchero scored a team-high 20 points. Orlando has won 10 of the last 15 encounters.
